scenes.tts: Strawberries, mushrooms, bacteria and people all have D N A. How can one kind of molecule help make such different living things? How can a tiny code inside my cells decide what I look like?
scenes.caption: Strawberries, mushrooms, bacteria and people all have DNA. How can one kind of molecule help make such different living things? How can a tiny code inside my cells decide what I look like?
scenes.visual: Four labelled blocks (strawberry, mushroom, bacterium, person) appear one by one, each gets a DNA tag; then the question appears in two lines.
scenes.narration: Strawberries, mushrooms, bacteria and people all have DNA. How can one kind of molecule help make such different living things? How can a tiny code inside my cells decide what I look like?

scenes.tts: D N A is a molecule. It carries the instructions for building proteins. Its shape is a twisted ladder. This shape is called a double helix. The two sides of the ladder are sugar and phosphate. The sides are the same in every living thing.
scenes.caption: DNA is a molecule. It carries the instructions for building proteins. Its shape is a twisted ladder. This shape is called a double helix. The two sides of the ladder are sugar and phosphate. The sides are the same in every living thing.
scenes.visual: DNA block arrow to proteins block; they clear and a flat ladder (two bars, four rungs) is built; labels: double helix (drawn flat), sugar and phosphate on both sides, same in every living thing.
scenes.narration: DNA is a molecule. It carries the instructions for building proteins. Its shape is a twisted ladder. This shape is called a double helix. The two sides of the ladder are sugar and phosphate. The sides are the same in every living thing.

scenes.tts: The code sits in the rungs. Each rung is a base pair: two bases joined in the middle. The four bases have letter names: A, T, C and G. A always pairs with T. C always pairs with G. So if one side reads A, C, G, T, the other side reads T, G, C, A.

scenes.visual: Rungs become pairs of coloured letter blocks; labels base and base pair; legend A T C G; A-T and C-G pairs flash; one side keeps A C G T, the other side goes to question marks and is filled in T G C A.
scenes.narration: The code sits in the rungs. Each rung is a base pair: two bases joined in the middle. The four bases have letter names: A, T, C and G. A always pairs with T. C always pairs with G. So if one side reads A, C, G, T, the other side reads T, G, C, A.

scenes.tts: The order of the bases is called the sequence. The sequence is the code. A different order gives different instructions. Think of letters in a word. The same letters in a new order spell a new word. But a cell does not understand words. Its molecules simply follow the bases in order.

scenes.tts: D N A is very long and thin. A chromosome is a strand of D N A wound up tightly with proteins. A gene is a section of a chromosome. A gene carries the code for a particular protein. A protein builds cells and does most of the work in cells. Proteins affect traits. A trait is a feature of a living thing, like flower colour.

A protein builds cells and does most of the work in cells. Proteins affect traits. A trait is a feature of a living thing, like flower colour.
scenes.visual: A long thin line becomes a thick bar (chromosome); one section lights up as a gene; a chain gene, protein, trait is built below with short descriptions.
scenes.narration: DNA is very long and thin. A chromosome is a strand of DNA wound up tightly with proteins. A gene is a section of a chromosome. A gene carries the code for a particular protein. A protein builds cells and does most of the work in cells. Proteins affect traits. A trait is a feature of a living thing, like flower colour.

scenes.tts: In pea plants, purple flowers need a working protein from one gene. A change in that gene can stop the protein from working. Then the flowers come out white. So how do strawberries, mushrooms, bacteria and people differ? They all build D N A from the same sugar, phosphate and four bases. The order of the bases differs, so their genes code for different proteins.
